title: Hi-Lo: card tags
subtitle: Update the count from cards, without independent-task hints.

theory.text: Hi-Lo tags are not blackjack points: 2–6 add +1; 7–9 add 0; 10, J, Q, K and A add −1. Start running count (RC) at zero after a shuffle and add each exposed card’s tag once. For example, 5 raises RC by one and K lowers it by one. A tag does not depend on its seat or whether the hand wins. Introductory cards show tags; practice hides them unless you ask for a hint, and independent tasks have no hints. Enter the sum of all tags, including the final two-card example. This is a closed training simulation, not an external table counter.

coaching.explanation: 5: (+1) = +1. Starting RC 0 plus this change gives +1. Neutral cards do not contribute; count each revealed card once.
coaching.contrast: Compare 2, K (0) with 2, 3 (+2): grouping saves effort, but the signs of the tags still matter.

title: Hi-Lo: count a chunk
subtitle: Update the count from cards, without independent-task hints.

theory.text: Read a chunk as one change in running count: add the tags of its 3–5 cards, then add that change to the starting count. For example, 2, 4, Q sum to +1; 2, 4, Q, A sum to 0. Neutral 7–9 do not change the sum. A chunk need not cancel to zero. Each group below appears at once so that you practise the group rather than use per-card feedback. On independent tasks no tags, cancellation markers or correct RC are shown. The cards and your first answer survive leaving the lesson.

theory.text: RC continues between hands: a new hand does not reset it. Only a shuffle resets the count. Each sequence here starts at the known count left by the preceding sequence. For example, RC +2 followed by A, 3, 7 stays +2. After a pause, return to the saved cards and last known checkpoint; do not count exposed cards twice or invent a missing count. In this lesson the starting checkpoint is explicit. The separate full-deck check hides true intermediate counts.

theory.text: A full deck ends at zero because Hi-Lo is balanced, but two mistakes can cancel. Therefore a zero ending cannot prove correct counting. Update a known checkpoint using only the cards exposed after it. For example, RC −3 plus 2, 4, K becomes −2, not +1. The full-deck check asks for RC after every eight cards and after card 52; any wrong checkpoint fails that attempt. The ordinary tasks below prepare the same calculation on short sequences.

theory.text: Accuracy comes first. Practise short sequences without a timer; then optionally open the separate full-deck check after completing this lesson. Three fresh complete decks must be correct at every checkpoint, successively within 60, 45 and 30 seconds of active interaction. Storage and background time are excluded. A failed count or missed deadline requires a fresh attempt from the first level. No hints, count tags or extra XP are provided by the check. This is an internal learning standard, not evidence of a financial edge.
